races.title: State Senate, District 21
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Tom McInnis
cands.bio: Thomas Moses McInnis, a Republican from Pinehurst, is a North Carolina state senator first elected in 2014. He founded Iron Horse Auction Company in 1983, served 8 years on the Richmond County Board of Education, and chairs the Senate Finance Committee.
cands.gaps: We found no documented stance from McInnis on data centers, homestead property tax elimination, limits on investor or foreign land buying, or slowing growth. We found no record on H-1B or immigration enforcement, or on police pay and pensions. His campaign site's list of what he has done is the campaign's own account and was not independently verified. Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for him in 2026. We found no reported controversies about him. The sources do not say when he moved to his current home in Pinehurst. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys.

local.label: Roots 100: Wikipedia says he was born in Richmond County, NC, and grew up on a working-class family farm there; Ballotpedia and his campaign site also say he grew up in Richmond County and now lives in Pinehurst.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: State senator since 2015; founded Iron Horse Auction Company in 1983 and works as its chief operations officer; served 8 years on the Richmond County Board of Education; former member of the Richmond County Planning and Zoning Board and Board of Elections; former chair of the Richmond County Economic Development Board.
qual.why: About 11 years of prior legislative service, plus business ownership and local elected and appointed county posts. Committee chair roles were not counted.
qual.label: About 11 years of prior legislative service, plus business ownership and local elected and appointed county posts. Committee chair roles were not counted.

second-amendment.evidence: Says on his campaign site that restricting lawful gun ownership is not the answer, and describes himself as a Life Member of the NRA.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Says on his campaign site that he has fought for higher pay for teachers and school personnel and will keep looking for ways to ensure parents can choose the best educational options for their children.

pro-life.evidence: His campaign site says he secured state appropriations for nonprofits in the district, including Life Care Pregnancy Center. This is the campaign's own claim and was not checked against budget records.

prio.label: Matches 3 of 3 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 3 only promised

cands.name: Paul Taylor
cands.bio: Democratic candidate for North Carolina State Senate District 21 in 2026. U.S. Army veteran who served 1977 to 1997. He describes himself as a nonprofit leader and community organizer. He has not held elected office, according to the sources available.

endorsements.text: Listed by Ballotpedia as receiving voter guide recommendations from three Sway voting groups: 'Reject AIPAC from City Council to Congress' (Vote for Peace), 'Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy' (Tevin Davis) and 'Waves of Democracy' (Terri Robinson).

cands.gaps: We could not find where Paul Taylor was born or raised, or when he came to North Carolina. We found no details on his nonprofit work, such as the organization or his role. We found no record of his work history beyond Army service from 1977 to 1997. His stated priorities are public education, the economy and healthcare, with an emphasis on clean air and water and reliable infrastructure. We found no specific stated positions or actions on data centers, property taxes, development, immigration, guns, abortion, school vouchers or policing. We found no documented stance on development or data centers. We found no documented controversies about him.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Served in the U.S. Army from 1977 to 1997. In his own words he is a nonprofit leader and organizer who has worked on youth programs and community initiatives. No elected or legislative office is documented.
qual.why: He has a 20-year military career but no documented legislative, policy, budget or business work and no prior elected office. The nonprofit work is self-described without specific roles, so it adds no score. That places him in the low range for a job that writes law and the state budget.
